examples: By the end of the year, the fifth graders will have learned about perfect tenses, correlative conjunctions, introductory elements, and Greek and Latin roots.
By June, the students will have mastered every grammar skill that was taught since the beginning of the year.

vocab.def: A standard or principle by which something may be judged or decided.
vocab.simple: A rule or measure you use to decide if something is good enough!
vocab.example: One criterion for a good essay is that it has a clear thesis statement.
vocab.starter: The most important criterion for _______ is...
vocab.why: Having clear criteria helps you judge quality and improve your own work!

sentences.orig: the students whom had worked so hard this year can now identify independent and dependant clauses use perfect tenses and write complex sentenses with confidance

corr.e: The first word of a sentence must be capitalized.
Use 'who' as a subject pronoun (the students did the working). 'Whom' is an object pronoun.
The correct spelling is 'dependent' with an e, not an a.
The correct spelling is 'sentences' with a c, not an s.
The correct spelling is 'confidence' with -ence at the end.

sentences.fixed: The students who had worked so hard this year can now identify independent and dependent clauses, use perfect tenses, and write complex sentences with confidence.

manip.task: Rewrite using correlative conjunctions to emphasize the range of skills mastered.
examples: The students who had worked so hard this year can not only identify independent and dependent clauses but also use perfect tenses and write complex sentences with confidence.
Both identifying clauses and writing complex sentences are skills the hardworking students have mastered this year.

vocab.def: The highest or final point of something; the climax.
vocab.simple: The big, exciting ending or the most important moment of something!
vocab.example: The science fair was the culmination of months of research and hard work.
vocab.starter: The culmination of our project was when...
vocab.why: Reaching a culmination means you have accomplished something great!

sentences.orig: wow this has been an incredable year because we have not only mastered grammer skills but we also growed as thinkers writers and communicaters

corr.e: Use a comma after an interjection like 'Wow' when it begins a sentence.
The correct spelling is 'incredible' with -ible, not -able.
The correct spelling is 'grammar' with -ar at the end.
The past participle of 'grow' is 'grown,' not 'growed.' Use 'have grown.'
Use commas to separate items in a series, and 'communicators' ends in -ors.

sentences.fixed: Wow, this has been an incredible year because we have not only mastered grammar skills but we also have grown as thinkers, writers, and communicators.

manip.task: Rewrite the sentence using all three perfect tenses to describe the year's journey.
examples: By last month, we had mastered most grammar skills; now we have grown as communicators; and by graduation, we will have become eloquent writers.
We had struggled at first, but we have persevered, and by the end of the year, we will have accomplished every goal.

vocab.def: Something handed down from the past; a lasting impact or contribution.
vocab.simple: The important things you leave behind for others to remember and use!
vocab.example: The great teacher left a legacy of students who love learning.
vocab.starter: The legacy I want to leave is...
vocab.why: Thinking about your legacy inspires you to make a positive difference!

sentences.orig: congratulations fifth graders you have accomplished something truely remarkable and weather you realize it or not you are now prepaired to succeed in midle school

corr.e: Use a comma for direct address and capitalize the first word of a sentence.
When adding -ly to 'true,' drop the final e: truly.
Use 'whether' as a conjunction meaning 'if.' 'Weather' refers to climate conditions.
The correct spelling is 'prepared' with -pared, not -paired.
The correct spelling is 'middle' with double d.

sentences.fixed: Congratulations, fifth graders! You have accomplished something truly remarkable, and whether you realize it or not, you are now prepared to succeed in middle school.

manip.task: Rewrite using all three perfect tenses to celebrate the past, present, and future achievements of the class.
examples: You had entered fifth grade as learners, you have accomplished something truly remarkable this year, and by the time you finish middle school, you will have become even more incredible.
Before this year, you had never imagined how far you could go; now you have proven yourselves; and in the future, you will have achieved even greater things.

vocab.def: To grow or develop in a healthy, vigorous way; to thrive.
vocab.simple: Growing strong and doing really well, like a plant in sunshine!
vocab.example: Students flourish when they have supportive teachers and engaging lessons.
vocab.starter: I flourish when...
vocab.why: Everyone can flourish when they have the right support and keep trying!
